rationale: D3 (#959): the lane enforced one-edge-per-pair for `uses` (`usesSeen`) and for nothing else. Measured over 554 real C++ files: 841 excess `contains` rows and 87 excess `references` rows, with `uses` at 0 — the set that existed was working, the two that did not exist were not. `contains` repeats a fact because constructors normalize to the single name `constructor` (the family contract, C# parity) while operator overloads keep their spelling, so a 14-overload constructor emitted 14 identical `person contains constructor` rows; every row is persisted and every row carries a line_number, so a consumer counting edges got a number that meant nothing. `references` repeats because an `#include` is a compile-time dependency and six `#include <vector>` lines express one. THIS FIXTURE ALSO PINS THE DISTINCTION the first cut of the register got wrong. That cut counted every repeated (source,type,target) row and reported 29,708; that number conflated two shapes and was wrong. `calls` is NOT deduped: line N calling `foo` and line M calling `foo` are two facts, each with its own M59.A7 `line_number`, and the C, TypeScript and Java lanes all emit both. So the three repeated `p.age()` calls at the bottom of `talker()` are pinned as EXPECTED, and a future 'fix' that deduped them would be a regression against the family contract, not an improvement. The overloads remain SYMBOLS — only the duplicated edge is dropped, so nothing resolvable stops being resolvable.  M14 ONTOLOGY (2026-10-04): the three `#include` rows below are now `imports` — C++'s file inclusion is a first-class `imports` edge, the same kind and metadata the C lane emits for the identical construct (c/macro-composed-include; reverted by the `c/include-kind-downgraded` mutant). The two `using` rows stay `references`, which is the measured distinction this fixture already draws for D3: an include dependency and a using-dependency name DIFFERENT targets (`vector` vs `std::vector`) and are two facts. The `references` label is forbidden on the include targets so a downgrade fails here and not only in a census.

expectSymbols.name: constructor
expectSymbols.note: the family normalization: 14 overloads are 14 SYMBOLS that share this name, each with its own range and line. Only the EDGE is deduplicated.

expectSymbols.name: age
expectSymbols.note: four `age` overloads -> four method symbols sharing this name.

expectRelationships.note: D3b: THREE `#include <vector>` lines, THREE imports pushed, ONE edge — and the edge takes the FIRST directive's line (23), because walk order is source order. 'How many times was it included' is a count the `imports` array keeps; 'what does this file depend on' is an edge.
D3b: the same, for the repeated `string` include.

D3b for `using`: the repeated `using std::vector;` states one dependency. The target is the module the `using` names (`std::vector`), which is deliberately a DIFFERENT edge from the `#include <vector>` one — an include dependency and a using-dependency are two facts.

M14 ONTOLOGY (2026-10-04), question 6. `calls` published NO `confidence` at all before this round, and it is the largest edge family in the lane: measured 101,340 `calls` rows over 929 corpus files, every one `undefined`, against a documentation table claiming 1.0. `confidenceMin: 1` is the assertion that catches its removal — and it was added because the mutant `cpp/ontology-calls-confidence-dropped` SURVIVED against the fixtures as they stood, which is the useful part of a mutation run. `evidenceClass: usage_contextual` is pinned in the same row because the two are decided in different places: the tier by the family classifier, the number by the writer. D3c: the measured distinction. SIX `age` call sites are SIX call facts, each with its own M59.A7 line_number (72, 73, 74, 77, 78, 79), and the C, TypeScript and Java lanes all emit every one. Deduplicating these would be a regression against the family contract, not an improvement — which is why the first cut of the register, reporting 29,708, was wrong.

D3a: 14 constructor overloads normalize to one name, so containment is ONE fact about the class. The edge lands on the FIRST declaration's line (36), which is the declaration a consumer navigating to the name wants.
four `age` overloads, one edge, first declaration's line.
14 overloads again, on a second class.
the `uses` position the existing `usesSeen` set already governed, unchanged by D3 — pinned so the two new sets are not confused with it. The source is the `age(int v)` method, which writes `age_`.

expectRelationshipCount.note: D3a, and WHY this block exists. `expectRelationships` means '>= 1 match', so a duplicated edge satisfies it and the whole class D3 is invisible to it — the first version of this fixture passed against the pre-fix analyzer for exactly that reason, and the mutation harness is what said so (`SURVIVED cpp/d3-duplicate-contains-and-references`). `equals` is an EXACT count, so this is the only form of the assertion that can fail on a duplicate. 14 constructor overloads normalize to one name, so containment is ONE fact about the class.
14 overloads again, on a second class — so the assertion is not specific to `Person`.

D3b: THREE `#include <vector>` lines, THREE imports pushed, ONE edge — and the edge takes the FIRST directive's line (23), because walk order is source order. 'How many times was it included' is a count the `imports` array keeps; 'what does this file depend on' is an edge.
the repeated `string` include, and the repeated `using std::string;` is a DIFFERENT target (`std::string`) so it is a different edge — an include dependency and a using-dependency are two facts.
the repeated `using std::vector;` states one dependency.

D3c, the measured distinction, pinned as an EXACT count of six. Six `age` call sites are SIX call facts, each with its own M59.A7 line_number, and the C, TypeScript and Java lanes all emit every one. A version that deduped them would land here as 1 and fail — which is the point: the first cut of the defect register deduped them, reported 29,708, and was wrong.

forbidRelationships.note: self-containment is impossible — a class does not contain itself.
D3 + the ontology: `contains` is REAL container ownership, and the global namespace is not a container. 'Never `global contains X`' is in the analyzer's contract.

#910-for-cpp: the include dependency carried as `references` + metadata.isImport. Forbidding the OLD label is what makes this a regression gate for a downgrade rather than a note about one — the same discipline c/macro-composed-include uses, and the reason a silent relabel cannot pass.
